issues.description: Fork-block initial base-fee returns for block fork+1 instead of fork block itself. Spec requires fork block itself to have INITIAL_BASE_FEE, with ongoing calculation thereafter. Code inverts this: fork block falls through to parent-based calculation (parent has no baseFee pre-fork) while second London block incorrectly resets to initial value.
issues.potential_impact: Consensus failure at fork activation: fork block rejected or miscalculated, second block baseFee reset incorrectly causing chain split from spec-compliant clients and invalid baseFeeValidation.
issues.suggestion: Change guard to `if (londonForkBlockNumber == blockNumber) return getInitialBasefee();` to match spec and execution-spec `if header.number != FORK_CRITERIA.block_number` logic.

issues.code_location: LondonFeeMarket.computeBaseFee: missing fork-block gas-target adjustment, no handling of parent gas_limit doubling
issues.description: Spec requires special casing on fork block to avoid halving gas target: parent_gas_target = parent.gas_limit and parent_gas_limit = parent.gas_limit * ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER. Implementation takes targetGasUsed as caller-supplied parameter with no fork adjustment and only special-cases fee value, so first ongoing calculation uses halved target (parent_limit // 2) instead of full parent_limit.
issues.potential_impact: Incorrect baseFee trajectory immediately after fork: baseFee increases even when parent used full pre-fork limit, causing consensus divergence from clients implementing spec fork logic and incorrect gasLimitValidation.
issues.spec_reference: # on the fork block, don't account for the ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER to avoid # unduly halving the gas target.
issues.suggestion: Implement fork-block target handling: when computing fee for block fork+1, use parent_gas_target = parent_gas_limit (not parent_gas_limit // ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER), and ensure gas-limit validation doubles parent limit on fork block.

issues.description: Introduces non-spec 7 wei floor: `DEFAULT_BASEFEE_FLOOR = Wei.of(7L)` and `satisfiesFloorTxFee` requires gasPrice or maxFeePerGas >= 7 wei. Spec has no floor; only checks are max_fee >= base_fee, max_fee >= max_priority_fee, max_fee < 2**256, and baseFee can decay toward zero. computeBaseFee does not enforce floor, so baseFee can go below floor while transactions are still filtered.
issues.potential_impact: Valid low-fee transactions that satisfy baseFee (e.g., baseFee 1 wei) rejected from mempool/validation, causing mempool divergence, censorship of valid transactions, and potential liveness stall if baseFee < floor but floor filter blocks all transactions. Consensus divergence if used for block validation.
issues.spec_reference: ensure that the user was willing to at least pay the base fee
issues.suggestion: Remove extra floor check for consensus validation; restrict it to optional local mempool spam policy only, and ensure baseFee calculation and block validation follow spec with no minimum other than spec delta logic.

verification.matched_excerpt: ensure that the user was willing to at least pay the base fee

issues.description: Spec fixes INITIAL_BASE_FEE = 1000000000. Implementation allows arbitrary override via genesis config including zero. No validation that override equals spec constant on mainnet fork.
issues.potential_impact: If configured differently, fork block baseFee mismatches spec-compliant clients leading to consensus split; zero initial value changes genesis economics and edge-case fee dynamics.
issues.suggestion: Enforce INITIAL_BASE_FEE = 1000000000 for spec networks or document override as test-only deviation and validate consistency across nodes.

summary: Core baseFee formula (denominator 8, slack 2, max 1-wei increase, parent-target logic) matches spec, but fork-block handling is off-by-one and misses elasticity special-case, and implementation adds non-spec 7-wei transaction floor and configurable initial baseFee. This file also does not implement gas-limit bounds, fee-cap/priority-cap checks, GASPRICE semantics, or baseFee burn which must be verified elsewhere.
